findings.message:
URL matching suppresses qualified issue-reference sanitization

`URL_START_RE` matches `www.` at any position, including inside a valid repository name. For example, `Fixes ubiquity/www.repo#123` is split at `www.`, so the keyword and qualifier are processed in separate slices and `Fixes` remains, allowing the published PR to retain an auto-close directive. URL detection must respect reference-token context or URL boundaries.

src/github/text.ts:11-11

Reference-style Markdown destinations are rewritten

Only inline `](...)` destinations are protected. A valid reference definition such as `[r]: /foo:fixes:#123` has no protected range, so the colon-aware regex removes `fixes:` and changes the URL to `/foo:#123`. This violates the stated byte-preservation behavior and the inline-relative-link policy; reference-style destinations also need protection.

summary: Two correctness issues remain in the sanitizer’s URL and Markdown protection logic.
